newsitem.title: USA: Chances of Democrat Congress improve - Reuter poll.
newsitem.headline: Chances of Democrat Congress improve - Reuter poll.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's popularity has boosted prospects that the Democrats could recapture one or both houses of Congress from Republican control, a Reuters poll said on Thursday.

The poll, conducted by John Zogby Group International, indicated that for the first time since Reuter polling began at the beginning of August a slight majority of voters favoured a return of Democratic majorities in Congress.
Republicans swept to majorities in both the House of Representatives and Senate in 1994 for the first time in 40 years.
The poll said 43.1 percent wanted Democrats to control the Senate against 41.9 percent favouring Republicans. In the House, 42.0 percent wanted Democrats against 41.2 percent for Republicans.
Those figures were within the poll's 3.2 percent margin of error but represented a sharp turnaround since the last Reuters poll of August 22 when Republicans held the lead.

The Reuters poll also said Clinton had widened the gap in the presidential race to 15 percentage points ahead of Republican challenger Bob Dole, from five points on August 22 poll and 12 points on August 6.
"Clinton has not only dramatically surged himself, but I think almost single-handedly raised voters' perceptions of Congressional Democrats," pollster John Zogby said.

The August 22 Reuters-Zogby poll said voters preferred Republicans in control of Congress -- by 43.6 percent to 36.6 percent in the Senate and 40.8 percent to 37.7 percent in the House. The August 6 poll showed similar preferences.
But Zogby said that, while the latest poll suggests Democrats have a chance of recapturing Congress, they are far from closing the deal. Much depended on the individual races.

"Democrats in Congress are not doing as well as their president is right now. They're just sort of tagging along," Zogby said. Meanwhile, Republican Congressional candidates are doing better than their presidential candidate, he said.

"Dole trails the Republican congressional candidates in every region and in just about every subgroup. Republicans are ahead (in Congressional races) in the West and the South, but Dole is behind," Zogby said.

Regionally, the poll said Democrats had widened their lead in Congressional preferences in the East, drawn closer to Republicans in the South and West, and drawn level in the critical central and Great Lakes states.
The poll, conducted from September 2-4, asked voters which party they would prefer to win a majority in the Senate and House respectively.
It differed from standard Congressional polls, which normally ask voters which candidate they plan to vote for in their Congressional district.
"It's asking them to go beyond their own district. It's more of a national mood question," Zogby said of the poll. Which party is your preference to win a majority in
the Senate and the House, respectively?
